data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's Condorcet/noise-cancellation mechanism rests on the premise that panelist judgments are 'independent draws,' but trained non-experts following the SAME explicit checklist are structurally correlated: the checklist is a shared deterministic function mapping each case's observable features to the same judgment. If two panelists apply identical checklist rules to the same case features, their errors are not independent idiosyncratic noise—they are shared systematic errors from checklist design (shared misreading, common training bias). The 1/√n variance reduction therefore does not apply. SRC_002's own counterconditions flag positive error correlation, yet its mechanism derivation still invokes Condorcet aggregation as the structural advantage, which is the false premise. The aggregation advantage is real only when errors are uncorrelated, which a common checklist actively undermines.
